units.text: INT. OBSERVATORY DOME - SÉANCE - NIGHT
A great brass telescope tilts toward a slit of stars.
A round oak table fills the center of the floor, ringed by four chairs.
A single candle gutters.
The dome creaks as it turns.
MADAME ZELDA VOSKUIJLEN (60s, turban, rings on every finger) presides, palms flat on the wood.

To her left sits PROFESSOR EDMUND HARTWELL (70s, astronomer, pocket watch); to her right, a YOUNG WOMAN in mourning grey (20s, veil pushed back); opposite, a MAN in a damp overcoat who has given no name (40s, gloved).
Hands joined. Breathe. Is there a presence among us?
units.name: MADAME ZELDA

units.text: The candle gutters.
Hartwell clears his throat.
My dear, is this strictly necessary?
units.name: HARTWELL

units.text: Hush.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: Is there a presence?
units.name: MADAME ZELDA

units.text: The telescope creaks as though a hand had nudged it.
The dome stills.
A single cold breath crosses the table.
Adelheid?
units.name: MAN

units.text: The Young Woman jerks her hand free.
Who said that?
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: Edmund, I mean, I did not.
units.name: HARTWELL

units.text: Silence! Hands!
units.name: MADAME ZELDA

units.text: It's not the dead who answer. It's the clock in your pocket, Professor.
units.name: MAN

units.text: Hartwell pulls out the pocket watch.
It is ticking backward.
This is not possible.
units.name: HARTWELL

units.text: The Young Woman stands, ripping off her veil.
She is not young.
She is ADELHEID HARTWELL (50s, his wife, long thought drowned), her face lit white by the candle.
Hello, Edmund.
units.name: ADELHEID

units.text: The Man removes his glove and lays a badge on the table.
Hartwell sways.
